verdict.rationale: Gitea Actions automations are written as YAML workflows. Gitea natively provides commit history and Pull Request/AGit code review, so automations kept as workflow files can plausibly be versioned and reviewed in-product. However, the evidence never explicitly ties workflow files to repo versioning, and it documents no rollback or revert mechanism for automations. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that workflow definitions are versioned in the repository, a documented rollback/revert path for automations, and hands-on corroboration of reviewing workflow changes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
browsing commit history and code files, reviewing and merging code submissions
Code review supports both the Pull Request workflow and AGit workflow.
